problem:
Consider the differential equation 

$$
{y}^{″}+7{y}^{′}+12y=g(x).
$$

The corresponding homogeneous equation has the fundamental solutions ${y}_{1}(x)={e}^{-3x}$ and ${y}_{2}(x)={e}^{-4x}:$According to the method of variation of parameters, we seek a particular solution of the form

$$
{y}_{p}(x)={{field-1}}
$$

where ${u}_{1}={u}_{1}(x),{u}_{2}={u}_{2}(x),$ that satisfies the constraint

$$
{y}_{p}^{′}(x)={{field-2}}.
$$

Substituting the expressions $y={y}_{p}$ and ${y}^{′}={y}_{p}^{′}$ into the differential equation yields the following relationship between ${u}_{1}^{′},{u}_{2}^{′},$ and $g(x):$

$$
{{field-3}}
$$
